content:
Cap Blanc rock shelter is an archaeological site located in Marquay, in the Dordogne department of southwestern France. It is renowned for its prehistoric art and is part of the UNESCO World Heritage-listed series of decorated caves in the Vézère Valley, significant for their Paleolithic art.

### Description and Location
The Cap Blanc rock shelter is situated on a hillside, carved into a long limestone cliff. This location made it an ideal shelter for prehistoric humans due to its natural protection elements and strategic viewpoint.

### Archaeological Significance
Cap Blanc is unique among the decorated caves of the Vézère Valley primarily due to its relief carvings, which stand out in contrast to the predominantly painted caves such as Lascaux and Chauvet. The art at Cap Blanc dates back to the Upper Paleolithic, specifically to the Magdalenian period (around 15,000 to 17,000 years ago).

### Artwork
The most striking feature of Cap Blanc is a frieze of sculpted animals, extending nearly 15 meters (49 feet) in length. This relief features a variety of animals, with the most prominent being equines and bison. The bison sculptures are particularly notable for their three-dimensional depth and realism. They protrude almost a meter from the wall in some places, showcasing an exceptional skill in manipulating the natural contours of the rock to enhance the visual effect of the carvings.

### Discovery and Excavations
The site was discovered in 1909, and systematic excavations began shortly thereafter. Over the years, archaeological investigations have provided insights into the construction techniques used by the Magdalenian people as well as their day-to-day life. Tools, hearths, and other artifacts have been found in addition to the artwork, pointing to the shelter being a place of both habitation and ritual artistic activity.

### Conservation
The preservation of the frieze at Cap Blanc has been a challenge due to its exposure to the elements, given that it is an open-air site rather than a deep cave like many others in the region. Efforts have been made to protect and conserve the artifacts and artwork from further degradation.

### Visitor Access
Cap Blanc is open to the public, offering guided tours that provide insight into the lives of the Magdalenian people and the significance of the carvings. The site presents a unique opportunity to view Paleolithic art in a context that differs from the more common cave paintings of the area.

Cap Blanc rock shelter remains an invaluable site for understanding the rich scope of prehistoric human expression and the artistic capabilities of early modern humans. Its sculptures are a testament to the complex cultural practices existing thousands of years ago, showing both artistic creativity and deep reverence for the natural world.
